data.note:
Specimen was lovastatin/mevinolin: PubChem CID 53232, ChEMBL CHEMBL503 HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (e28). Literature confirms HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor MoA class (PMID:3076125, PMID:12539818), annotated in BBBC021 as Cholesterol-lowering. My final call Actin disruptors was wrong.

Phenotype trap: mid-high doses showed strong actin heterogeneity/contrast and cell contraction with multinucleation, then extreme tubulin/actin bundling and shrinkage at high dose - visually and quantitatively mimicking direct cytoskeletal drugs. But statins block mevalonate -> loss of geranylgeranylation and Rho protein function (PMID:9758637) and Rho GTPase regulation/translocation (PMID:11120702, PMID:11406567, PMID:15982657), producing secondary actin reorganization and rounding. I mistook this downstream phenocopy for primary actin disruption, reinforced by mid-dose atlas match to cytochalasin and high-dose match to taxol/epothilone, and by the PI steer toward actin.

Lesson: retain Cholesterol-lowering when actin changes co-occur with small-nuclei/contraction without classic mitotic arrest, and test mevalonate add-back rescue plus HMGCR / prenylation readouts rather than only tubulin vs actin discrimination.

reflection.text:
We chased extreme high-dose texture: tub_glcm_contrast z=+66.8 and act_glcm_contrast z=+41.7 at 15 uM with only 69 cells left (e3), plus monotonic tub_mean rho=+1.00 (e10), tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 (e11) and act_std rho=+1.00 (e16) led first to Microtubule stabilizers 0.68 and then, after review pressure without new wells, to Actin disruptors 0.70. The unblinded identity mevinolin/lovastatin is an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor cholesterol-lowering agent (PMID 3076125, PMID 12539818), a class absent from the reference atlas.

The atlas vote of Microtubule stabilizers 7/10 (e6, e13) versus Actin disruptors 3/10 on mid-dose alone (e14) plus conflicting microscopy (e4 bundles vs e5 actin) should have signaled secondary cytoskeletal remodeling, not direct binding. Statin blockade of the mevalonate pathway impairs geranylgeranylation and Rho-protein function (PMID 9758637) and blocks RhoA translocation (PMID 11406567), which explains why actin heterogeneity, cell shrinkage rho=-1.00 (e18) and cell-count loss rho=-1.00 (e19) mimicked actin disruptors.

Acquisition choices amplified the error: starting with 1.5 uM and 15 uM emphasized toxic, low-cell-count secondary contraction, and we spent budget on 4 wells with only tubulin/actin dose-responses and no cholesterol, mevalonate-rescue, or prenylation readout to test an upstream metabolic mechanism.
what_was_right: Detected a real, monotonic dose-dependent cytoskeletal response: act_std rho=+1.00, act_mean rho=+1.00, tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 across 4 wells (e15, e16, e11).
Noted conflicting visual and atlas signals: high-dose bundles mapping to stabilizers (e4, e6) vs mid-dose actin aggregates mapping partly to actin disruptors/Eg5 (e5, e14).
Recognized high-dose toxicity with falling cell count rho=-1.00 and cell_area rho=-1.00 (e18, e19) and weak mitotic/multinucleate trends (e12 rho=+0.60 p=0.4, e17 rho=+0.40 p=0.6).
what_was_wrong: Misread extreme high-dose tub_glcm_contrast z=+66.8 and act_glcm_contrast z=+41.7 at 15 uM (e3) as direct microtubule stabilization, then as direct actin disruption, rather than secondary Rho/prenylation remodeling downstream of HMG-CoA reductase inhibition.
Overweighted 7/10 Microtubule stabilizer atlas neighbors (e6, e13) despite the atlas having no cholesterol-lowering reference and mid-dose alone shifting to Actin disruptors 3/10 (e14).

Flipped final call from Microtubule stabilizers 0.68 to Actin disruptors 0.70 (e20, e25, e26) after review without acquiring the requested dose-index-4 replicate-2 well, citing only existing actin dose-response (e23).

citations.claim: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors act through inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase as their defining cholesterol-lowering mechanism.
HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor effects involve geranylgeranylation and Rho proteins, linking statins to cytoskeletal regulation.
HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors inhibit RhoA translocation, providing a mechanism for secondary actin phenotypes without direct actin binding.

reflection.next_experiment: Mevalonate / geranylgeranyl-pyrophosphate add-back rescue in the same imaging assay plus HMG-CoA reductase-dependent cholesterol readout and RhoA prenylation/localization, with latrunculin (actin) and paclitaxel (microtubule stabilizer) as direct-target controls.

The unblinded identity mevinolin/lovastatin is an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor cholesterol-lowering agent (PMID 3076125, PMID 12539818), a class absent from the reference atlas.

The atlas vote of Microtubule stabilizers 7/10 (e6, e13) versus Actin disruptors 3/10 on mid-dose alone (e14) plus conflicting microscopy (e4 bundles vs e5 actin) should have signaled secondary cytoskeletal remodeling, not direct binding. Statin blockade of the mevalonate pathway impairs geranylgeranylation and Rho-protein function (PMID 9758637) and blocks RhoA translocation (PMID 11406567), which explains why actin heterogeneity, cell shrinkage rho=-1.00 (e18) and cell-count loss rho=-1.00 (e19) mimicked actin disruptors.

Acquisition choices amplified the error: starting with 1.5 uM and 15 uM emphasized toxic, low-cell-count secondary contraction, and we spent budget on 4 wells with only tubulin/actin dose-responses and no cholesterol, mevalonate-rescue, or prenylation readout to test an upstream metabolic mechanism.

What was right:
- Detected a real, monotonic dose-dependent cytoskeletal response: act_std rho=+1.00, act_mean rho=+1.00, tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 across 4 wells (e15, e16, e11).
- Noted conflicting visual and atlas signals: high-dose bundles mapping to stabilizers (e4, e6) vs mid-dose actin aggregates mapping partly to actin disruptors/Eg5 (e5, e14).
- Recognized high-dose toxicity with falling cell count rho=-1.00 and cell_area rho=-1.00 (e18, e19) and weak mitotic/multinucleate trends (e12 rho=+0.60 p=0.4, e17 rho=+0.40 p=0.6).

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread extreme high-dose tub_glcm_contrast z=+66.8 and act_glcm_contrast z=+41.7 at 15 uM (e3) as direct microtubule stabilization, then as direct actin disruption, rather than secondary Rho/prenylation remodeling downstream of HMG-CoA reductase inhibition.
- Overweighted 7/10 Microtubule stabilizer atlas neighbors (e6, e13) despite the atlas having no cholesterol-lowering reference and mid-dose alone shifting to Actin disruptors 3/10 (e14).
- Flipped final call from Microtubule stabilizers 0.68 to Actin disruptors 0.70 (e20, e25, e26) after review without acquiring the requested dose-index-4 replicate-2 well, citing only existing actin dose-response (e23).

Proposed next experiment: Mevalonate / geranylgeranyl-pyrophosphate add-back rescue in the same imaging assay plus HMG-CoA reductase-dependent cholesterol readout and RhoA prenylation/localization, with latrunculin (actin) and paclitaxel (microtubule stabilizer) as direct-target controls.
